citeAs: Zayene, M., Endres, J., Havolli, A., Corbière, C., Cherkaoui, S., Kontouli, A., Alahi, A. (2025). HELVIPAD: A Real-World Dataset for Omnidirectional Stereo Depth Estimation. arXiv:2411.18335.
creator: Mehdi Zayene, Jannik Endres, Albias Havolli, Charles Corbière, Salim Cherkaoui, Alexandre Kontouli, Alexandre Alahi (EPFL, Switzerland; TU Darmstadt, Germany)
description: HELVIPAD is a real-world dataset for omnidirectional stereo depth estimation, featuring 39,553 labeled video frames from 29 video sequences across diverse indoor and outdoor environments on a university campus, under varied lighting conditions including day and night. Data were collected using two Ricoh Theta V 360° cameras in a top-bottom setup with a 19.1 cm baseline and a synchronized Ouster OS1-64 LiDAR sensor, providing accurate depth and disparity labels by projecting 3D point clouds onto equirectangular images. An augmented training set with increased label density via depth completion is also provided.
name: HELVIPAD
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Custom automated pipeline using Robot Operating System (ROS) on an embedded NVIDIA Jetson Xavier for data capture and synchronization; LiDAR-to-image projection and depth completion implemented as custom software pipelines.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Depth and disparity labels were generated automatically by projecting LiDAR point clouds onto equirectangular images. The projection pipeline involved: (1) selecting key 3D points on a 19×19 chessboard for calibration, (2) applying initial rotation and translation transformations, (3) converting to spherical coordinates, (4) projecting onto the equirectangular plane, and (5) optimizing rotation and translation parameters by minimizing pixel error using BFGS. Disparity values were derived from depth values using the spherical disparity formula. Projection accuracy was validated by manually selecting 200 random LiDAR points and computing Euclidean distances to their image positions, yielding an average error of 1.7 pixels (8.0 pixels in visually challenging areas).
rai:dataBiases: The dataset was collected exclusively on a university campus, which may not fully represent all urban environments. The depth completion pipeline increases the density of low-range depth values (particularly within the 0–10 meter range), enriching the representation of closer objects. A distinct concentration of short-range distances within the 0–10 meter range is attributed to the LiDAR laser capturing the ground surface. The dataset exhibits an exponential decay in pixel percentage with increasing depth, correlating with decreased LiDAR precision over longer distances. Night outdoor scenes are underrepresented compared to daytime scenes.
rai:dataCollection: Data were collected using a custom-built rig equipped with two Ricoh Theta V 360° cameras in a top-bottom setup with a 19.1 cm baseline, capturing equirectangular images at 30 fps at an initial resolution of 3840×1920 pixels, paired with an Ouster OS1-64 LiDAR sensor (64 beams, 42.4° vertical FOV, operating at 10 fps) mounted 45.0 cm below the bottom camera. The rig was mounted on a custom-built, remotely controlled robot chassis. Data were collected across 29 video sequences in indoor (corridors, halls) and outdoor (squares, external parking, footpaths) settings on a university campus, under diverse weather and lighting conditions. A central processor (NVIDIA Jetson Xavier) managed data capture and ensured device synchronization via hardware-triggered flash synchronization.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data consists of 29 video sequences of paired equirectangular images from two Ricoh Theta V 360° cameras (top and bottom) captured at 30 fps at 3840×1920 pixels resolution, synchronized with LiDAR point clouds from an Ouster OS1-64 sensor operating at 10 fps. Sequences were recorded between December 2023 and February 2024 across indoor and outdoor settings on a university campus.
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset was collected on a university campus, which may limit generalization to other environments. The depth completion method does not provide labels at object boundaries, and minor discrepancies may be present in measured point clouds at boundaries. The temporal aggregation approach for depth completion is limited for fast-moving objects like cars. LiDAR point clouds are sparse, especially for objects at far range. Occlusions between the LiDAR and cameras were not explicitly handled. The dataset does not include odometry information.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: An augmented training set was created using a depth completion pipeline tailored for 360° images. The pipeline performs temporal aggregation (fusing the current frame's LiDAR point cloud with those from the 4 preceding and 4 succeeding frames), spherical interpolation using k=17 nearest neighbors with inverse-distance weighting, and filtering based on uncertainty and out-of-distribution thresholds (RIP=0.8). This increased the ratio of labeled pixels from approximately 12% to 61%. Photometric data augmentation was also applied during model training.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Camera frames were subsampled to match the LiDAR frame rate (10 fps) by retaining one out of every three camera frames. LiDAR point clouds were projected onto equirectangular images via an optimized rotation and translation transformation (minimizing pixel error using BFGS optimization). After mapping, depth values were converted to spherical disparity in degrees. Top and bottom images, depth maps, and disparity maps were cropped to remove unnecessary borders (sky, ground) and downsampled from a width of 1024 pixels to 512 pixels. The resulting dataset comprises 39,553 paired images at 1920×512 pixels resolution.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset supports development of depth estimation systems for mobile robots operating in dynamic human environments, with applications in autonomous driving, healthcare robotics, and agricultural robotics. The dataset captures pedestrian activity in public spaces, enabling research into robot navigation and interaction with humans.
rai:dataUseCases: Developing and benchmarking omnidirectional stereo depth estimation models; robotic navigation and exploration in complex indoor and outdoor environments; assessing robustness of depth estimation methods to diverse lighting conditions and depth ranges; cross-scene generalization studies for depth estimation in dynamic human environments.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: KISS-ICP (LiDAR odometry algorithm based on ICP) was evaluated for temporal aggregation in the depth completion pipeline. The final depth completion pipeline uses a custom automated spherical interpolation and filtering approach without KISS-ICP (no-movement temporal aggregation was selected as the best approach).
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset contains video frames of dynamic human environments with pedestrians present (average of 13.33 pedestrians in indoor sequences and 17.65 pedestrians in outdoor sequences). No explicit mention of anonymization or privacy measures for individuals captured in the scenes.

null_reasons.license: No license information is mentioned in the paper.
null_reasons.rai:annotationsPerItem: Labels are generated automatically from LiDAR projection; no concept of multiple independent annotations per item applies.
null_reasons.rai:annotatorDemographics: Annotation is fully automated via LiDAR projection pipeline; no human annotators involved.
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: No inter-annotator agreement analysis; annotation is automated. Projection quality is assessed via pixel error metrics (reported separately as part of calibration validation).
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: No explicit discussion of missing data handling beyond the depth completion pipeline (which is a manipulation protocol, not missing data imputation).
null_reasons.rai:dataImputationProtocol: No imputation of missing values in the dataset itself; depth completion is a label augmentation technique, not imputation of missing sensor data.
null_reasons.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: No versioning, update cadence, or maintenance plan described in the paper.
